_doc: Pixel post parameters (07_ASSET_PIPELINE.md section 2.5). Changing any value is a director-visible decision because every sheet must be rebuilt. Reduction: each scale x scale block of the 4x render becomes one 1x pixel. A 4x sample counts as covered when its alpha >= alpha_threshold; the 1x pixel is opaque when at least coverage_min_samples of the block are covered, and its colour is the integer-rounded mean RGB of the covered samples (a box filter, which does the work of 07's 0.5 px pre-blur plus nearest). The mean is then mapped to the nearest palette colour by squared RGB distance, ties to the lowest palette index, with no dithering. Output alpha is binary (0 or 255) and transparent pixels are written as 0,0,0,0. ramps_by_layer limits a layer to some ramps (per-ramp protection: body shading lands only in the neutral skin ramp; soot is drawn, never quantised to, because grey soot inside the figure read as mud: Lead QC round 2). After quantising, despeckle_layers merge dark blotches inside the figure (a 4-connected run of one colour, at most despeckle_max_px pixels, darker than everything bordering it) into the most common bordering colour (Lead QC 2026-10-09, rounds 1 and 2). Then the outline (06 section 3): opaque pixels with a transparent 4-neighbour take the outline colour (ramp step); drawn on the figure's own edge, so silhouette, pivot and normal-map alpha do not change. With --parts (a render_character.py parts pass) the same colour is drawn inside the figure on arm pixels that touch body pixels, the 06 inner line where the silhouette would merge (Lead QC round 2).
